schema.question: str
schema.accept: array of lowercase strings a grader should mark correct

questions.question: What is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.hint: It alone covers about an eighth of the world's inhabited land.

questions.question: Mount Everest sits on the border between which two countries?
questions.hint: One side calls the peak Sagarmatha, the other Chomolungma.

questions.question: Which strait separates Spain from Morocco?
questions.hint: Barely 13 km across at its narrowest; a famous rock guards its north side.

questions.question: Which two countries share the longest international border?
questions.hint: Nearly 9,000 km of it, much drawn along the 49th parallel.

questions.question: What is the capital of Mongolia?
questions.hint: The world's coldest capital, in a landlocked country of steppe.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.hint: One of only three countries entirely enclosed by a single other.

questions.question: Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake, lies in which country?
questions.hint: It holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

questions.question: Counting its overseas territories, which country spans the most time zones?
questions.hint: Its scattered overseas departments stretch from the Pacific to the Caribbean.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in South America by area?
questions.hint: A former Dutch colony on the northeast shoulder of the continent.

questions.question: The Bosphorus strait runs through which major city?
questions.hint: The only city sitting on two continents at once.

questions.question: Which gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.hint: Inert enough that we breathe it in and out unchanged.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.hint: Two letters, from the Latin 'aurum'.

questions.question: How many chambers does a human heart have?
questions.hint: Two on top that receive, two below that pump.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle carries a negative charge?
questions.hint: It orbits the nucleus and carries the current in a wire.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.hint: Named after a German physicist; its symbol is the last Greek letter.

questions.question: Which planet has the shortest day in our solar system?
questions.hint: The biggest planet also spins the fastest — under ten hours.

questions.question: What is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust?
questions.hint: About 8% of the crust, and we wrap food in it.

questions.question: What is the scientific study of fungi called?
questions.hint: From the Greek 'mykes'; it covers mushrooms and moulds.

questions.question: Which naturalist independently arrived at a theory of natural selection at the same time as Charles Darwin?
questions.hint: His letter from Indonesia forced Darwin to publish.

questions.question: What is the name for the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
questions.hint: Two words; cross it and even light cannot come back.

questions.question: In what year did the Titanic sink?
questions.hint: Two years before the First World War began.

questions.question: Who was the first female Prime Minister of the United Kingdom?
questions.hint: In office 1979-1990, nicknamed the Iron Lady.

questions.question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched into orbit?
questions.hint: Soviet, launched 1957; its beeping started the space race.

questions.question: Which empire reached its height under Suleiman the Magnificent?
questions.hint: It ruled from Constantinople for six centuries.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone was the key to deciphering which writing system?
questions.hint: The same text appeared on it in Greek, which unlocked the rest.

questions.question: Which treaty formally ended the First World War between Germany and the Allies?
questions.hint: Signed in a palace hall of mirrors in 1919.

questions.question: The Opium Wars were fought between Britain and which country?
questions.hint: Britain fought to keep selling the drug there.

questions.question: In which century did the Black Death sweep through Europe?
questions.hint: The 1340s, when perhaps a third of Europe died.

questions.question: Who led the early victories of the Haitian Revolution against French colonial rule?
questions.hint: A formerly enslaved general who beat Napoleon's army.

questions.question: The Meiji Restoration, which rapidly modernized the country, took place in which nation?
questions.hint: It ended two and a half centuries of shogunate rule in 1868.

questions.question: Which author created the detective Hercule Poirot?
questions.hint: A Belgian detective with a formidable moustache and 'little grey cells'.

questions.question: Which Russian novelist wrote Crime and Punishment?
questions.hint: He spent four years in a Siberian prison camp.

questions.question: In Nineteen Eighty-Four, what is the name of the Party's ever-watching figurehead?
questions.hint: Two words; his face is on every telescreen.

questions.question: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude?
questions.hint: A Colombian Nobel laureate; the town is called Macondo.

questions.question: What was George Orwell's real name?
questions.hint: He took his pen name from a river in Suffolk.

questions.question: Which Japanese novelist wrote Norwegian Wood and Kafka on the Shore?
questions.hint: A Beatles song title gave one of those novels its name.

questions.question: Which author wrote the Discworld fantasy series?
questions.hint: A flat world carried on four elephants standing on a turtle.

questions.question: Which Chinese classic novel follows the monk Xuanzang and the Monkey King on a pilgrimage west?
questions.hint: One of the Four Great Classical Novels; a pilgrimage to fetch scriptures.

questions.question: Which Nigerian author wrote Things Fall Apart?
questions.hint: Its title comes from a Yeats poem.

questions.question: Which epic poem opens with the narrator lost in a dark wood, midway through life's journey?
questions.hint: Written in Italian in the early 1300s; Virgil guides the narrator.

questions.question: Who directed the animated film Spirited Away?
questions.hint: It won the Best Animated Feature Oscar in 2003.

questions.question: In The Matrix, which colour pill does Neo swallow?
questions.hint: The other choice would have sent him back to sleep.

questions.question: What is the name of the fictional nation ruled by T'Challa in Black Panther?
questions.hint: Hidden behind a holographic shield, rich in vibranium.

questions.question: Which TV series is set in the fictional town of Hawkins, Indiana?
questions.hint: The 1980s, a girl with a shaved head, and a monster world called the Upside Down.

questions.question: In Breaking Bad, what alias does Walter White use?
questions.hint: Taken from the physicist of the uncertainty principle.

questions.question: Which Hong Kong director made In the Mood for Love and Chungking Express?
questions.hint: Known for smeared step-printed slow motion and Christopher Doyle's camera.

questions.question: Which Stanley Kubrick film is set aboard the spacecraft Discovery One?
questions.hint: Its computer sings 'Daisy Bell' as it is shut down.

questions.question: Which South Korean director won Best Director for Parasite?
questions.hint: He also made Memories of Murder and Snowpiercer.

questions.question: Which martial arts star's real name was Lee Jun-fan?
questions.hint: He died in 1973, weeks before Enter the Dragon opened.

questions.question: Which film won the very first Academy Award for Best Picture?
questions.hint: A silent film about First World War fighter pilots.

questions.question: How many keys does a standard full-size piano have?
questions.hint: Fifty-two white and thirty-six black.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.hint: Tuned in fifths: G, D, A and E.

questions.question: Which Beatles album cover shows the band on a zebra crossing?
questions.hint: Named after the London street where the studio stands.

questions.question: Which band released The Dark Side of the Moon?
questions.hint: A prism splitting white light on the sleeve.

questions.question: In musical notation, what does 'forte' instruct a performer to do?
questions.hint: Its opposite marking is 'piano'.

questions.question: How many semitones are there in an octave?
questions.hint: The number of keys, white and black, from one C to the next.

questions.question: What is the name of the two-stringed Chinese bowed instrument often called the 'Chinese violin'?
questions.hint: Two words; the bow is threaded between the strings.

questions.question: Which composer died leaving his Requiem unfinished?
questions.hint: A rival was rumoured, wrongly, to have poisoned him.

questions.question: Which Chinese plucked zither, typically with 21 strings, is played flat on a stand?
questions.hint: Two words; moveable bridges sit under each string.

questions.question: What is the term for a piece of music performed without instrumental accompaniment?
questions.hint: Italian, and it means 'in the manner of the chapel'.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in hummus?
questions.hint: A pulse, blended with tahini, lemon and garlic.

questions.question: What spirit forms the base of a mojito?
questions.hint: The same spirit as a daiquiri, with mint and lime added.

questions.question: What is tofu made from?
questions.hint: Curdled and pressed, the way cheese is made from milk.

questions.question: Which country produces more coffee than any other?
questions.hint: It has led the world since the 1840s, and Vietnam is second.

questions.question: What is the Korean dish of fermented, seasoned cabbage called?
questions.hint: Buried in earthenware pots to ferment through the winter.

questions.question: Which spice, harvested from crocus stigmas, is the most expensive in the world by weight?
questions.hint: It takes about 150 flowers to yield a single gram.

questions.question: Dim sum is most closely associated with which region of China?
questions.hint: The province around Guangzhou, where the tea-house tradition began.

questions.question: What type of dough is used to make profiteroles and éclairs?
questions.hint: The same dough is piped to make gougères and croquembouche.

questions.question: What is the Japanese term for the savoury 'fifth taste'?
questions.hint: Identified by Kikunae Ikeda in 1908; glutamate is what triggers it.

questions.question: Which tea is traditionally smoked over pinewood fires, giving it a distinctive smoky flavour?
questions.hint: From the Wuyi Mountains in Fujian; it tastes of campfire.

questions.question: Who painted The Starry Night?
questions.hint: Painted from an asylum window at Saint-Rémy in 1889.

questions.question: Which art movement is Salvador Dalí most associated with?
questions.hint: Melting clocks, lobster telephones, and a waxed moustache.

questions.question: Michelangelo's David is carved from what material?
questions.hint: Quarried at Carrara, from a block other sculptors had abandoned.

questions.question: Which architect designed Barcelona's Sagrada Família?
questions.hint: Still unfinished after more than 140 years.

questions.question: Which Japanese artist created the woodblock print The Great Wave off Kanagawa?
questions.hint: From the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

questions.question: What is the term for painting applied directly onto wet plaster?
questions.hint: The pigment binds as the plaster dries, so you cannot correct it.

questions.question: Which contemporary artist is famous for polka dots and mirrored 'Infinity Rooms'?
questions.hint: A Japanese artist who has lived voluntarily in a psychiatric institution since 1977.

questions.question: Which architectural style is defined by pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses?
questions.hint: It succeeded Romanesque and gave us Notre-Dame and Chartres.

questions.question: Which museum in Paris is home to the Venus de Milo?
questions.hint: Also home to the Mona Lisa and a glass pyramid.

questions.question: What term describes the shophouse-style walk-up tenement buildings characteristic of old Hong Kong?
questions.hint: Two Cantonese words for the narrow pre-war blocks with balconies over the pavement.

questions.question: How many players from one team are on the pitch in a football (soccer) match?
questions.hint: Ten outfield players plus the one in gloves.

questions.question: In chess, which piece moves only diagonally?
questions.hint: It stays on its starting colour for the whole game.

questions.question: In tennis, what word is used for a score of zero?
questions.hint: Possibly from the French for egg, after the shape of a nought.

questions.question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
questions.hint: Five titles, more than anyone else, and the only country at every finals.

questions.question: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.hint: Front nine plus back nine.

questions.question: Which Olympic event combines swimming, cycling, and running?
questions.hint: Three disciplines in one race, finishing on foot.

questions.question: In the board game Go, what are the playing pieces called?
questions.hint: Black and white, placed on intersections rather than squares.

questions.question: How many tiles does each player hold on their rack in Scrabble?
questions.hint: One fewer than a Scrabble bingo needs to use them all plus a board letter.

questions.question: Which martial art, now an Olympic sport, originated in Korea and emphasizes kicking?
questions.hint: Its name translates roughly as 'the way of the foot and fist'.

questions.question: In cricket, what is the term for a bowler taking three wickets on three consecutive deliveries?
questions.hint: The same term football uses for three goals, but far rarer.

questions.question: What is the term for a word that reads the same forwards and backwards?
questions.hint: 'Racecar' and 'level' both qualify.

questions.question: What do you call a word that imitates the sound it describes, like 'buzz' or 'clang'?
questions.hint: Comic books are full of them: pow, splat, whoosh.

questions.question: Which alphabet is used to write Russian?
questions.hint: Named after a 9th-century missionary saint.

questions.question: How many letters are in the Greek alphabet?
questions.hint: It runs from alpha to omega — two more than English has minus two.

questions.question: What is the study of the origin and history of words called?
questions.hint: Not what a word means now, but where it came from.

questions.question: The abbreviation 'e.g.' stands for which Latin phrase?
questions.hint: Two Latin words meaning roughly 'for the sake of example'.

questions.question: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.hint: Over a billion speakers, concentrated in one country.

questions.question: Esperanto was created in the 1880s as what kind of language?
questions.hint: Invented by L. L. Zamenhof so no nation would own it.

questions.question: The Cantonese term 'dim sum' translates literally to roughly what phrase?
questions.hint: A poetic phrase about the organ that beats, not the stomach.

questions.question: What is the linguistic term for a word borrowed directly from another language, like 'kindergarten' or 'ballet'?
questions.hint: English is stuffed with them: 'ballet', 'karaoke', 'kindergarten'.

questions.question: What does 'CPU' stand for?
questions.hint: Often called the computer's brain; it executes the instructions.

questions.question: What does 'RAM' stand for?
questions.hint: Volatile working memory — it empties the moment power is lost.

questions.question: In 'HTTPS', what does the S stand for?
questions.hint: It is what the padlock icon in the address bar is promising.

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
questions.hint: A British scientist who built it at CERN in 1989.

questions.question: Which programming language was created by Guido van Rossum?
questions.hint: Named after a British comedy troupe, not the snake.

questions.question: Which version control system was created by Linus Torvalds?
questions.hint: He wrote it in 2005 to manage the Linux kernel's source.

questions.question: What does 'SQL' stand for?
questions.hint: The language you are writing when you type SELECT.

questions.question: Which 19th-century mathematician is often called the first computer programmer for her notes on the Analytical Engine?
questions.hint: Daughter of the poet Byron; collaborated with Charles Babbage.

questions.question: What is the decimal number 8 written in binary?
questions.hint: Four binary digits, and the value is a power of two.

questions.question: Which console generation is the SNES part of, commonly described by its processor bit-width?
questions.hint: Successor to an 8-bit machine, with the bit-width doubled.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.hint: Named after the swift messenger of the Roman gods.

questions.question: How many degrees are in a circle?
questions.hint: The Babylonians chose it because it divides so many ways.

questions.question: Which zodiac sign is represented by a pair of scales?
questions.hint: The only zodiac sign represented by an object, not a living thing.

questions.question: What is the currency of Switzerland?
questions.hint: Not the euro — the country stayed out.

questions.question: What is the collective noun for a group of owls?
questions.hint: A nod to their reputation for wisdom.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.hint: One systemic, and one for each set of gills.

questions.question: What is the traditional gift associated with a 25th wedding anniversary?
questions.hint: The same metal as the second-place medal.

questions.question: How many minutes are there in a full week?
questions.hint: Sixty times twenty-four times seven.

questions.question: What is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world?
questions.hint: Named after an American aviator who crash-landed on top of it.

questions.question: In Chinese numerology, which number is widely considered lucky because it sounds like the word for 'prosperity'?
questions.hint: It sounds like the word for wealth, which is why buildings skip other floors.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.hint: A compromise: neither Sydney nor Melbourne got it.

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.hint: It covers more of the planet than all the land combined.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.hint: You could walk across it in twenty minutes; it has a Swiss Guard.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent?
questions.hint: Home to about 60% of humanity.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.hint: Not Toronto, and not Montreal.

questions.question: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
questions.hint: Its own name for itself, Nihon, means roughly the same thing.

questions.question: Which US state is the largest by area?
questions.hint: More than twice the size of the second-largest.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in the world above sea level?
questions.hint: Measured from sea level, not from the Earth's centre.

questions.question: What is the longest river in the world?
questions.hint: It flows north, through eleven countries.

questions.question: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.hint: Roughly the area of the United States, and it is growing.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.hint: Purpose-built inland in the 1950s, shaped like an aeroplane from above.

questions.question: How many member states are in the European Union?
questions.hint: It was 28 before one member left in 2020.

questions.question: The Dead Sea borders which two countries?
questions.hint: The West Bank lies between them.

questions.question: Which African country famously resisted European colonisation and was never fully colonised?
questions.hint: It defeated an Italian invasion at Adwa in 1896.

questions.question: In which country would you find the Great Wall?
questions.hint: It runs for thousands of kilometres and is not, in fact, visible from space.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.hint: Two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen.

questions.question: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.hint: A baby has far more; many fuse as we grow.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.hint: Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.hint: Iron oxide dust gives it the colour.

questions.question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.hint: Around two square metres of it, and it weighs several kilos.

questions.question: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.hint: One fewer since 2006.

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level, in Celsius?
questions.hint: The top of the Celsius scale as originally defined.

questions.question: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
questions.hint: It scores 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.hint: About eight light-minutes away.

questions.question: Which organelle is often called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.hint: It has its own DNA and was probably once a separate organism.

questions.question: Which scientist developed the theory of general relativity?
questions.hint: He published it in 1915, a decade after the special theory.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
questions.hint: Two letters, from the Latin 'argentum'.

questions.question: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
questions.hint: It lacks both A and B antigens and the Rh factor.

questions.question: What does DNA stand for?
questions.hint: Three words; the middle one is the sugar in its backbone.

questions.question: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.hint: Fast enough to circle the Earth seven times in a second.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.hint: He was followed down the ladder twenty minutes later by Buzz Aldrin.

questions.question: In which year did the Second World War end?
questions.hint: Two surrenders that year, in May and in August.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.hint: He refused a third term, setting a precedent that held for 150 years.

questions.question: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.hint: A centennial gift, designed by Bartholdi with a frame by Eiffel.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.hint: The same year as Tiananmen and the Velvet Revolution.

questions.question: Which US president was assassinated in Dallas in 1963?
questions.hint: Shot from a book depository while riding in an open car.

questions.question: In which year did the First World War begin?
questions.hint: It began after an assassination in Sarajevo that June.

questions.question: What was the name of the ship that carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620?
questions.hint: It sailed from Plymouth; a compact was signed aboard.

questions.question: Who was the principal author of the US Declaration of Independence?
questions.hint: He was 33 at the time and later became the third president.

questions.question: Which civilisation built Machu Picchu?
questions.hint: An Andean empire, conquered by Pizarro a century after building it.

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the movable-type printing press in Europe?
questions.hint: A goldsmith from Mainz; his Bible was the first major book printed.

questions.question: Which Egyptian queen was famously involved with both Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
questions.hint: The last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

questions.question: Who led the Soviet Union during the Second World War?
questions.hint: He took the name meaning 'man of steel'.

questions.question: Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
questions.hint: He also wrote Hamlet and Macbeth.

questions.question: Who wrote the Harry Potter series?
questions.hint: She wrote the first book in Edinburgh cafés as a single mother.

questions.question: Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?
questions.hint: It opens with a line about a single man in possession of a good fortune.

questions.question: Who created Sherlock Holmes?
questions.hint: A Scottish doctor who tried to kill the character off at a waterfall.

questions.question: Who wrote The Lord of the Rings?
questions.hint: An Oxford philologist who invented the languages first.

questions.question: Who wrote The Great Gatsby?
questions.hint: He also wrote Tender Is the Night; his wife was Zelda.

questions.question: Who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird?
questions.hint: She published almost nothing else for over fifty years.

questions.question: Who wrote Frankenstein?
questions.hint: Written for a ghost-story contest at Lake Geneva when she was eighteen.

questions.question: What is the first book of the Bible?
questions.hint: It begins 'In the beginning'.

questions.question: Who wrote The Old Man and the Sea?
questions.hint: A Cuban fisherman, a marlin, and eighty-four days without a catch.

questions.question: Which Spanish author wrote Don Quixote?
questions.hint: He lost the use of his left hand at the Battle of Lepanto.

questions.question: Who played Jack Dawson in Titanic?
questions.hint: He finally won an Oscar for The Revenant, decades later.

questions.question: Which film franchise features the line 'May the Force be with you'?
questions.hint: George Lucas created it; the first film came out in 1977.

questions.question: What is the name of Harry Potter's pet owl?
questions.hint: A snowy owl, delivered as a birthday present from Hagrid.

questions.question: Which animated Disney film features a lion cub named Simba?
questions.hint: Its plot borrows heavily from Hamlet.

questions.question: What is the name of the coffee shop the friends hang out in on Friends?
questions.hint: An orange sofa, and Gunther behind the counter.

questions.question: Which studio produced Toy Story?
questions.hint: Steve Jobs bought it from Lucasfilm before it made the film.

questions.question: Which actor played Iron Man in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
questions.hint: He was largely uninsurable before the role turned his career around.

questions.question: Who directed Jaws?
questions.hint: The mechanical shark broke down so often it barely appears.

questions.question: Who directed Pulp Fiction?
questions.hint: It tells its story out of chronological order, in chapters.

questions.question: Which film pairs FBI trainee Clarice Starling with Dr. Hannibal Lecter?
questions.hint: It swept all five major Oscars in 1992.

questions.question: What is the longest-running American animated sitcom?
questions.hint: It has aired since 1989 and is set in Springfield.

questions.question: Which 2009 James Cameron film is set on the moon Pandora?
questions.hint: The highest-grossing film of all time, twice over.

questions.question: In The Wizard of Oz, what city is Dorothy trying to reach?
questions.hint: Follow the yellow brick road, and it is the colour of the gem.

questions.question: Which singer is known as the King of Rock and Roll?
questions.hint: He recorded at Sun Studio in Memphis and lived at Graceland.

questions.question: How many members were in The Beatles?
questions.hint: John, Paul, George and Ringo.

questions.question: Who recorded the album Thriller?
questions.hint: The best-selling album of all time, released in 1982.

questions.question: Which country did the band ABBA come from?
questions.hint: The name is an acronym of the four members' first names.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.hint: Two more than a violin has.

questions.question: Which famous composer continued writing music after going deaf?
questions.hint: He conducted the premiere of his Ninth and could not hear the applause.

questions.question: Which Italian composer wrote The Four Seasons?
questions.hint: A red-haired priest who taught at a Venetian orphanage.

questions.question: Which instrument was Louis Armstrong famous for playing?
questions.hint: Nicknamed Satchmo; he also sang 'What a Wonderful World'.

questions.question: Who wrote and performed 'Like a Rolling Stone'?
questions.hint: He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016.

questions.question: What is the national anthem of the United States?
questions.hint: The lyrics come from a poem written during the War of 1812.

questions.question: Which British band released the song 'Bohemian Rhapsody'?
questions.hint: Six minutes long, with an operatic section and no chorus.

questions.question: Which fruit is used to make wine?
questions.hint: Trodden, pressed and left to ferment.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.hint: A stone fruit, botanically a berry, mashed with lime and onion.

questions.question: Which country is pizza traditionally associated with?
questions.hint: Naples in particular claims the modern form.

questions.question: What bean is chocolate made from?
questions.hint: It is fermented, dried and roasted before it becomes a bar.

questions.question: What do bees produce?
questions.hint: They regurgitate and evaporate flower nectar to make it.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in an omelette?
questions.hint: Beaten, then set in a pan without stirring.

questions.question: What scale is used to measure the heat of chili peppers?
questions.hint: Named after the American pharmacist who devised it in 1912.

questions.question: Which nut is the main ingredient in marzipan?
questions.hint: Ground with sugar into a paste; marzipan is mostly this and sugar.

questions.question: Meat from a calf is known by what name?
questions.hint: A young animal, giving pale, tender meat.

questions.question: Which country is the origin of sushi?
questions.hint: It began as a way of preserving fish in fermented rice.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.hint: It hangs behind bulletproof glass and is smaller than most expect.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.hint: He considered himself a sculptor and resented the commission.

questions.question: In traditional colour theory, what are the three primary colours?
questions.hint: Mix any two and you get orange, green or purple.

questions.question: Which artist is famous for his Campbell's Soup Cans?
questions.hint: He also silkscreened Marilyn and predicted fifteen minutes of fame.

questions.question: Who sculpted The Thinker?
questions.hint: Originally conceived as Dante, sitting above the Gates of Hell.

questions.question: Who painted Guernica?
questions.hint: A monochrome protest at the bombing of a Basque town in 1937.

questions.question: Which artist painted The Persistence of Memory, with its melting clocks?
questions.hint: Ants, a barren landscape, and time going soft.

questions.question: How many players from one team are on a basketball court at once?
questions.hint: Two guards, two forwards, one centre.

questions.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.hint: One for each inhabited continent, interlocked.

questions.question: Which sport is played at Wimbledon?
questions.hint: Grass courts, strawberries and cream, all-white clothing.

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
questions.hint: The same interval as a US presidential term.

questions.question: In which sport would you use a puck?
questions.hint: Played on ice, with a rubber disc instead of a ball.

questions.question: Which sport is nicknamed 'the beautiful game'?
questions.hint: Pelé used the phrase as the title of his autobiography.

questions.question: Which boxer famously called himself 'The Greatest'?
questions.hint: He lit the Atlanta Olympic flame in 1996 and refused the Vietnam draft.

questions.question: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
questions.hint: The country that invented the ancient games hosted the revival.

questions.question: In ten-pin bowling, what is three strikes in a row called?

questions.question: Which English composer wrote the orchestral suite The Planets?
questions.hint: Seven movements, one per planet known at the time, minus Earth.

questions.question: The aria 'Summertime' comes from which Gershwin opera?
questions.hint: An American folk opera set in Catfish Row, Charleston.

questions.question: Which Russian composer wrote the piano suite Pictures at an Exhibition?
questions.hint: Written in memory of a friend's exhibition; Ravel orchestrated it.

questions.question: 'O Fortuna' opens which 20th-century cantata by Carl Orff?
questions.hint: Set to medieval Latin and Middle High German poems.

questions.question: Which English composer wrote the Enigma Variations?
questions.hint: Fourteen portraits of his friends, with a hidden theme he never revealed.

questions.question: Which American composer wrote the Adagio for Strings used in the film Platoon?
questions.hint: Adapted from the slow movement of his own string quartet.

questions.question: Which Baroque composer wrote the Canon in D, a wedding staple?
questions.hint: Baroque, German, and the piece was obscure until the 1970s.

questions.question: Which Italian composer wrote the opera Aida, set in ancient Egypt?
questions.hint: Commissioned for Cairo, around the time the Suez Canal opened.

questions.question: Which Puccini opera is set in Nagasaki and centres on Cio-Cio-San?
questions.hint: A US naval officer, a fifteen-year-old bride, and a betrayal.

questions.question: The aria 'Nessun dorma' comes from which Puccini opera?
questions.hint: Set in Peking; the prince must solve three riddles.

questions.question: Which Rossini overture became the theme for The Lone Ranger?
questions.hint: A Swiss folk hero and an apple on a boy's head.

questions.question: Which Rossini comic opera features the barber Figaro singing 'Largo al factotum'?
questions.hint: A prequel, in story terms, to Mozart's Marriage of Figaro.

questions.question: Which Hungarian virtuoso composed the Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2?
questions.hint: He invented the solo piano recital and was mobbed like a pop star.

questions.question: Which numbered Schubert symphony is known as the 'Unfinished'?
questions.hint: It has only two completed movements, and nobody knows why.

questions.question: Mahler's Symphony No. 8 is nicknamed the Symphony of a what?
questions.hint: The nickname counts the performers at its vast 1910 premiere.

questions.question: Shostakovich's Symphony No. 7, written during a WWII siege, is nicknamed after which city?
questions.hint: He wrote it while the city was encircled; the score left on microfilm.

questions.question: Which Rachmaninoff piano concerto, his second, became a concert-hall staple after his recovery from depression?
questions.hint: Dedicated to the hypnotherapist who treated his writer's block.

questions.question: Niccolò Paganini was a legendary virtuoso on which instrument?
questions.hint: He was so agile that rumours spread he had sold his soul.

questions.question: Which Aaron Copland ballet score incorporates the Shaker tune 'Simple Gifts'?
questions.hint: Set in the Appalachians; Martha Graham choreographed it.

questions.question: 'The Moldau' (Vltava) belongs to which Smetana cycle of symphonic poems?
questions.hint: Six symphonic poems about Bohemian landscape and legend.

questions.question: Which eccentric French composer wrote the spare, hypnotic Gymnopédies?
questions.hint: He founded a one-member church and left 84 identical handkerchiefs.

questions.question: The Baroque period in music is conventionally dated from roughly 1600 to which year?
questions.hint: The year its greatest composer died, which is how the boundary was drawn.

questions.question: Which stylistic period followed the Classical era in Western music?
questions.hint: It brought bigger orchestras, programme music and national schools.

questions.question: What distinguishes a concerto from a symphony?
questions.answer: A concerto features a solo instrument set against the orchestra
questions.hint: One of them puts a single player in dialogue with the whole ensemble.

questions.question: What is the orchestral piece that opens an opera called?
questions.hint: It plays before the curtain rises.

questions.question: What is the written text of an opera called?
questions.hint: Italian for 'little book'.

questions.question: The 'Polovtsian Dances' come from which composer's opera Prince Igor?
questions.hint: A chemist by profession, and one of the Mighty Handful.

questions.question: Which Austrian painter created the gold-leaf masterpiece 'The Kiss'?
questions.hint: Vienna, 1908, and the two figures are wrapped in gold leaf.

questions.question: Which French sculptor carved the marble 'The Kiss', originally part of a larger commission?
questions.hint: It began as part of the same commission as his seated thinker.

questions.question: Which subject did Claude Monet paint roughly 250 times, drawn from his own garden pond?
questions.hint: He painted his own pond at Giverny again and again.

questions.question: In which French village did Monet create his famous garden and lily pond?
questions.hint: In Normandy, where he built the Japanese bridge.

questions.question: Monet painted more than thirty canvases of which cathedral façade at different times of day?
questions.hint: In Normandy, and he rented a room opposite to paint the façade.

questions.question: Besides cathedrals and lilies, Monet made a celebrated series depicting which stacked farm subject?
questions.hint: Stacks of harvested cereal, painted across the seasons.

questions.question: Which Italian Renaissance painter created 'The Birth of Venus'?
questions.hint: A goddess arriving on a shell, painted in Florence around 1485.

questions.question: Which Dutch master painted 'The Night Watch'?
questions.hint: A militia company portrait, and the darkness turned out to be varnish.

questions.question: Who painted 'American Gothic', showing a farmer with a pitchfork beside a woman?
questions.hint: The models were his sister and his dentist.

questions.question: Which American painter created 'Nighthawks', showing late-night customers in a diner?
questions.hint: A corner diner at night, seen through a curved window.

questions.question: Which Belgian surrealist painted 'The Son of Man', a bowler-hatted man with a floating green apple?
questions.hint: A Belgian who also painted a pipe that was not a pipe.

questions.question: Magritte's painting of a pipe labelled 'this is not a pipe' bears what actual title?
questions.hint: Its title is about representation itself, not about smoking.

questions.question: Which Spanish court painter created 'Las Meninas'?
questions.hint: He painted himself into the canvas, at his easel.

questions.question: Who painted 'The Third of May 1808', depicting the execution of Spanish resisters?
questions.hint: A man in a white shirt with his arms flung up before a firing squad.

questions.question: 'Saturn Devouring His Son' belongs to which grim late series by Goya?
questions.hint: Painted directly onto the walls of his own house.

questions.question: The painting popularly called 'Whistler's Mother' is formally titled 'Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1'. Who painted it?
questions.hint: An American in London who insisted the picture was about arrangement, not sentiment.

questions.question: Who painted 'Christina's World', showing a woman in a field looking toward a farmhouse?
questions.hint: The woman had polio; the house is in Maine.

questions.question: Which English landscape painter created 'The Hay Wain'?
questions.hint: A cart in a shallow river in Suffolk.

questions.question: Which English Romantic painted 'The Fighting Temeraire', showing a warship towed to be scrapped?
questions.hint: A ghostly white sailing ship under tow by a steam tug.

questions.question: Which German Romantic painted 'Wanderer above the Sea of Fog'?
questions.hint: A figure seen from behind, standing on a rocky outcrop.

questions.question: Who painted 'The Raft of the Medusa', based on a real shipwreck scandal?
questions.hint: Survivors of a French naval wreck, abandoned on a makeshift float.

questions.question: Which Neoclassical painter created 'Napoleon Crossing the Alps'?
questions.hint: The horse rears; the reality was a mule.

questions.question: Which Impressionist painted 'Bal du moulin de la Galette', a sunlit Parisian dance scene?
questions.hint: Dappled sunlight through the trees in Montmartre.

questions.question: Which Post-Impressionist painted the series 'The Card Players'?
questions.hint: Provençal peasants at a table, painted five times.

questions.question: Cézanne painted which Provençal mountain more than sixty times?
questions.hint: A limestone ridge near Aix-en-Provence.

questions.question: Which artist built 'A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte' entirely from tiny dots?
questions.hint: Parisians on an island in the Seine, built from optical dots.

questions.question: Which Post-Impressionist abandoned France to paint in Tahiti and the Marquesas?
questions.hint: He left a stockbroking career and died in French Polynesia.

questions.question: Van Gogh painted a celebrated series of still lifes featuring which flower?
questions.hint: Painted in Arles to decorate a room for a visiting friend.

questions.question: Which Van Gogh painting shows a yellow-lit café under a star-filled sky in Arles?
questions.hint: Painted in Arles; the terrace is still there today.

questions.question: Klimt's 'Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I' is popularly known by what name?
questions.hint: The Nazis seized it; a long restitution case followed.

questions.question: Which period of Picasso's career immediately followed his Blue Period?
questions.hint: Warmer tones, harlequins and circus performers.

questions.question: Which 1907 Picasso painting of five figures is seen as the opening of Cubism?
questions.hint: Five figures from a Barcelona brothel street, faces borrowed from African masks.

questions.question: Which Duchamp painting scandalised the 1913 Armory Show by fragmenting a figure in motion?
questions.hint: Motion broken into overlapping planes; a critic called it an explosion in a shingle factory.

questions.question: Which Dutch artist is known for grid compositions in black lines with red, yellow, and blue blocks?
questions.hint: De Stijl, and the compositions are named after boogie-woogie.

questions.question: Which American artist pioneered drip painting, working on canvases laid on the floor?
questions.hint: He worked from all four sides, calling it action painting.

questions.question: Which painter is most identified with large canvases of soft-edged, stacked rectangles of colour?
questions.hint: Their arrangement is meant to be viewed from very close up.

questions.question: Which Dalí painting shows the crucifixion viewed from above, without nails or blood?
questions.answer: Christ of Saint John of the Cross
accept: christ of saint john of the cross
christ of st john of the cross
questions.hint: Based on a drawing by a 16th-century Spanish friar.

questions.question: Which Frida Kahlo painting shows two versions of herself seated side by side, hearts exposed?
questions.hint: One in European dress, one in Tehuana, connected by an artery.

questions.question: Which Michelangelo sculpture shows Mary cradling the body of Christ?
questions.hint: Carved when he was 24; the only work he ever signed.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek sculptor created the original 'Discobolus', the discus thrower?
questions.hint: The bronze original is lost; only Roman marble copies survive.

questions.question: Which Venetian Renaissance painter created 'Bacchus and Ariadne'?
questions.hint: The god leaps from his chariot; the sky is lapis blue.

questions.question: Which Flemish painter created 'The Arnolfini Portrait', with its convex mirror?
questions.hint: A merchant, his wife, and a signature saying the painter was here.

questions.question: Which Flemish painter depicted 'The Tower of Babel' as a vast spiralling ruin?
questions.hint: A Flemish painter who set the biblical tower in a Antwerp-like port.

questions.question: Which painting hides a distorted skull that resolves only when viewed from the side?
questions.answer: The Ambassadors, by Hans Holbein the Younger
questions.hint: Two envoys, a table of instruments, and anamorphosis.

questions.question: Which contemporary artist created the giant mirror-polished 'Balloon Dog' sculptures?
questions.hint: Stainless steel made to look like a party balloon.

questions.question: Which anonymous street artist created 'Girl with Balloon'?
questions.hint: A stencil that shredded itself at auction in 2018.

questions.question: Which Pre-Raphaelite painted 'Ophelia', showing her drowning among flowers?
questions.hint: The model posed in a bath and caught a chill.

questions.question: Which ukiyo-e artist created the print series 'The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō'?
questions.hint: Post stations along the road between Edo and Kyoto.

questions.question: Which Romanian sculptor created the sleek bronze 'Bird in Space'?
questions.hint: So abstract that US customs taxed it as a metal object, not art.

questions.question: Which artist duo installed 'The Gates', 7,500 saffron fabric panels through Central Park?
questions.hint: A married pair who also wrapped the Reichstag.

questions.question: Which painter created 'A Bar at the Folies-Bergère', with its puzzling mirror reflection?
questions.hint: A barmaid, a marble counter, and a reflection that does not add up.

questions.question: Which Rococo painter created 'The Swing', showing a woman kicking off her slipper?
questions.hint: A bishop pushes the swing; a young man watches from below.

questions.question: Which ornate, playful 18th-century style is characterised by pastel colours and asymmetric curves?
questions.hint: It followed the Baroque and preceded Neoclassicism.

questions.question: Which sculptor cast a celebrated bronze 'David' decades before Michelangelo carved his?
questions.hint: The first freestanding nude bronze cast since antiquity.

questions.question: Who created the Florence Baptistery doors that Michelangelo called the Gates of Paradise?
questions.hint: Ten gilded bronze panels, and he spent 27 years on them.

questions.question: Which Amsterdam museum houses 'The Night Watch'?
questions.hint: The national museum on Museumplein, reopened in 2013 after a decade.

questions.question: Which Florence gallery houses 'The Birth of Venus'?
questions.hint: Its name means 'offices'; it was built for Medici administration.

questions.question: Which Madrid museum houses Picasso's 'Guernica'?
questions.hint: It returned from New York in 1981, after Franco's death.
